abstracts.value: The formulation of quantum measurements compatible with relativistic causality is obstructed by the tension between the locality of observable algebras and the dynamical state transformations induced by measurement processes. We develop a local measurement theory for quantum cellular automata, lattices of finite-dimensional quantum systems with a causal reversible dynamics evolving in discrete time steps. Measurement processes are described by localized completely positive maps and organized into operational measurement protocols, finite non-adaptive sequences of local instruments distributed across the causal cone induced by the automaton local dynamics. Each protocol induces an effective measurement on the initial time slice, whose support is constrained by the causal structure generated by the automaton. Non-local measurement effects therefore arise through causal propagation and composition of local operations, rather than from primitive non-local interventions or instantaneous collapse prescriptions. We establish the corresponding spatial support bounds and characterize the resulting measurement architecture. As an explicit example, we construct a two-step protocol for a one-dimensional nearest-neighbour qubit automaton which, for suitable automaton parameters, realizes a Bell-basis projective measurement on two neighbouring sites after coarse-graining of the local outcomes. Away from this point, the same protocol generates a continuous family of deformed Bell measurements whose entanglement and stabilizer Rényi non-classicality can be quantified explicitly. The framework thus provides a causally consistent operator-algebraic mechanism for synthesizing spatially extended quantum measurements from strictly local operations.

titles.title: Local Measurement Theory for Quantum Cellular Automata

abstracts.value: We apply gravitational path integral factorization to provide a semiclassical interpretation of generalized black hole free energy landscapes at fixed external temperature and angular velocities. Boundary integral transforms express the formal partition function as an integral over constrained sectors labeled by complete local partial-Neumann data on an auxiliary hypersurface. Independent variation establishes paired regular subregion solutions as constrained instantons, with Lagrange multipliers supporting lapse and tangential shift jumps that accommodate thermal and rotational mismatches. For selected nonextremal stationary families with an asymptotic boundary, the constrained saddle action takes the form $I_{\rm constr}=β\mathcal F_{\rm gen}=β(E_{\mathcal B}-Ω_{\mathcal B}^{I}J_{\mathcal B,I})-S$, with $β=T^{-1}$. Here $E_{\mathcal B}$ and $J_{\mathcal B,I}$ are renormalized Hamiltonian charges and $S$ is the black hole entropy, whose contribution to the action comes from the regular horizon cap. Interior stationary points of the landscape correspond to smooth equilibrium saddles when the retained variations independently span the entropy and angular momentum directions. We extend the construction to local, parity-even $f(\mathrm{Riemann})$ theories without curvature derivatives by retaining the complete auxiliary interface data. The same thermodynamic form follows with Wald entropy, without a small-deficit expansion. Schwarzschild and Kerr black holes illustrate the Einstein construction, while five-dimensional static AdS black holes in Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet gravity and the rotating BTZ branch of new massive gravity provide explicit checks of the higher-curvature extension.

abstracts.value: Elliptic flow ($v_2$) is the most prominent signature of collective flow in heavy-ion collisions. abstracts.value: Beam-induced backgrounds contribute to the trigger and data-acquisition rate at high-luminosity electron-positron colliders. abstracts.value: In the standard cosmological paradigm, the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum from a cosmic string network is well defined. However, early-Universe dynamics can significantly alter this relic signal. We systematically investigate how different new physics epochs in the radiation era--including extra relativistic degrees of freedom, early matter domination, intermediate vacuum domination, and kination--modify string network evolution and loop production. We find that a kination era enhances the stochastic GW signal, whereas the other scenarios suppress the signal to varying degrees. We also demonstrate that late-time dynamical dark energy has a negligible impact on the GW spectrum from cosmic strings.

titles.title: Impact of cosmic evolution on the gravitational wave spectrum from cosmic strings

abstracts.value: Rényi multi-entropy probes multi-partite structure beyond bipartite spectra, but its behavior in general quantum states and the entanglement structure it captures remain poorly understood. We develop a finite field Gauss sum framework for calculating it in stabilizer states. Within this framework, the replica contraction reduces to a quadratic Gauss sum if and only if the state is locally unitarily equivalent to a stabilizer state. We obtain analytic expressions for the Rényi multi-entropy of all tree graph states and large families of loop graph states. In contrast to their flat bipartite Rényi spectra, stabilizer states generically have nonflat Rényi multi-entropy spectra.

titles.title: Rényi Multi-entropy for Stabilizer States: A Finite Field Gauss Sum Problem

abstracts.value: Using 284 pb$^{-1}$ of $e^{+}e^{-}$ collision data collected with the BESIII detector at center-of-mass energies between 3.00 and 3.12 GeV, the relative phase between the strong and electromagnetic interaction amplitudes in the process $J/ψ\to Σ^+ \barΣ^-$ is determined. The relative phase is measured to be $(107.9 \pm 24.9)^{\circ}$ or $(-107.6 \pm 24.3)^{\circ}$, where the uncertainty includes both statistical and systematic sources. This is the first experimental determination of the strong-electromagnetic phase difference in $J/ψ$ decays to a hyperon-antihyperon pair. The branching fraction $\mathcal{B}_{J/ψ\to Σ^+ \barΣ^-}$ is measured to be $(1.14 \pm 0.04)\times 10^{-3}$ for the positive phase solution or $(1.19 \pm 0.04) \times 10^{-3}$ for the negative phase solution. These results provide important input for testing perturbative QCD predictions and studies of SU(3) flavor symmetry.

titles.title: Measurement of the relative phase between the strong and electromagnetic amplitudes in $\boldsymbol{J/ψ\to Σ^{+} \barΣ^{-}}$

abstracts.value: Scientific experiments often rely on deficient simulators and hardware whose commanded settings differ from the states realized in practice, limiting reliable optimization and inference. A Bayesian online calibration framework is introduced for experiments with at least one directly measurable simulator output and potentially latent quantities of scientific interest. Pre-calibration data are used to learn state-dependent effective simulator parameters, while a normalizing flow enables amortized posterior inference from measurement histories. During calibration, measurement and positioning uncertainties are propagated, and hardware commands are selected by balancing expected improvement with information gain. The framework is applied to the MADMAX dark matter experiment, where measured reflectivity is used to calibrate a deficient disk-booster simulator and infer the unobservable axion-signal power boost factor. Experimental validation on the MADMAX experiment is ongoing.

titles.title: Neural Bayesian Online Calibration with Deficient Simulators for MADMAX Dark Matter Experiment

abstracts.value: We investigate particle motion, optical observables, and linear wave propagation around a static black hole in Palatini Kalb Ramond gravity with a vanishing cosmological constant. The analysis distinguishes the conserved mass $M$ from the orbital mass $\bar{M}=M/ρ$ and isolates the radial deformation $σ^2=1-q/2$, where $q=\ell_2/(1-\ell_1)$. At fixed $\bar{M}$, the photon sphere, critical impact parameter, and innermost stable circular orbit retain their Schwarzschild values. Radial frequency ratios also preserve their Schwarzschild profiles for the same areal release and particle radii, while proper distances, infall times, and accumulated orbital angles depend on $σ$. For radial fall, the tidal eigenvalues acquire a factor $σ^{-2}$, and the instability exponent of the photon orbit scales as $σ^{-1}$. In addition, we examine light deflection in the weak and strong regimes with an explicit account of the conical asymptotics. The shadow comparison with Sgr A* and M87* exhibits a coupling degeneracy when the orbital mass and areal distance are set. Scalar, electromagnetic, and massless Dirac perturbations probe the physical metric, whereas a homogeneous axial gravitational sector with $δB_{μν}=0$ admits an exact Schwarzschild spectral map. In this sector, both oscillation and attenuation rates scale as $σ^{-1}$ at fixed $\bar{M}$. Third order WKB estimates agree with frequencies extracted from time evolution to within $0.7\%$ for the reported fundamental modes.

titles.title: Gravitational fingerprints of a black hole solution in Palatini Kalb-Ramond gravity

abstracts.value: Finite boundary drives ending at the same charge density can select different relaxation channels. We demonstrate this in a probe Abelian--Higgs model on a fixed AdS black brane with a stable normal endpoint. Charge exchange during preparation modifies scalar propagation and source coupling. Density history and radial Maxwell feedback during and after the drive leave a cubic slow amplitude even after linear slow-mode cancellation. For the tested protocols at $ρ_f=3$, the density-history term interferes constructively with the net radial feedback; its modulus is 85--89% of that of the total cubic coefficient. Calculated from the low-order equations alone, this total coefficient predicts the compensating pulse. Full nonlinear evolution confirms the reduction from $O(ε^3)$ to $O(ε^5)$ in the source amplitude $ε$, with approximately 600-fold suppression for the representative protocol at $ε=0.05$. Compensation extends the window of fast-channel relaxation without changing the final quasinormal-mode spectrum; early distance crossing already arises from linear interference. Fully tuned two- and three-pulse preparations suppress one and two slow modes, respectively, within numerical resolution. Local analysis establishes finite-pulse reachability of strong Mpemba states with vanishing selected asymptotic slow-mode coefficients. Charge-neutral controls retain a total-time advantage from a common input when the full subsequent control duration is included.

titles.title: Boundary preparation of strong Mpemba states in holography

abstracts.value: A spherically symmetric standing wave confined within a finite-radius ball, with weak radiative exchange between its core and boundary, provides a model for an intermediate stage in the adiabatic evolution of the $ϕ^4$ oscillon. We employ a multiscale variational framework to derive an approximate description of these standing waves and their energy-frequency relation. The resulting dispersion curve is compared with that obtained from numerical solutions of the boundary value problem for the $ϕ^4$ equation on a two dimensional (time and radius) domain. The agreement between the numerical and variational results is excellent near the endpoint of the continuous spectrum but deteriorates as $ω$ is reduced below $0.85 ω_0$. We attribute this discrepancy to the growth of the radiation wing, which is neglected in the variational ansatz.

titles.title: Dispersion of three-dimensional oscillons: a standing-wave perspective

abstracts.value: This work is motivated by two independent considerations. The first is that KNO scaling is observed in the central rapidity region ($|η|<0.5$, for example) and violated when the fragmentation region is included ($|η|<3.4$, for example). The second is that, in the CGC framework, the $k_T$-factorization formalism is more appropriate to describe particle production in the central region and the hybrid formalism is more appropriate for the fragmentation region. The former contains small-x gluon interactions, where the latter introduce also collinear gluons and valence quarks in the dynamics. These two considerations put together raise the natural question: are collinear gluons and valence quarks responsible for KNO scaling violation? To answer this question we build a two-component CGC model which is able to reproduce the measured pseudorapidity distributions over all the available range as well as multiplicity distributions in pp collisions at LHC energies. With this model we find that KNO scaling occurs when the interaction is dominated by small-x gluons but is broken by the interactions including small-x gluons, collinear gluons and valence quarks.

titles.title: KNO scaling violation: the role of the fragmentation region

abstracts.value: We present new hairy stationary and axisymmetric black hole solutions. These solutions belong to a subclass of Horndeski scalar-tensor theories, in which there is no non-minimal coupling to curvature. The full rotating solutions are obtained numerically using the Kadath library based on spectral methods. The metric does not rely on an explicit ansatz but rather on the use of a set of numerical coordinates. Black holes obtained differ from Kerr in general, and depend on a new independent parameter, a primary hair, coming from a linear time dependence in the scalar field. These solutions admit a Killing horizon like the Kerr black hole, but are non-circular, and break the zeroth law of black hole thermodynamics.

titles.title: A new class of rotating black hole solutions endowed with a scalar hair

abstracts.value: High-precision theoretical predictions for both signal and background processes are crucial for the precision physics program at the LHC and HL-LHC. A prime example is the determination of the effective leptonic weak mixing angle from neutral current Drell-Yan via template-fit methods, where Monte Carlo templates directly serve as input to the measurement, making theoretical uncertainties part of the systematic error affecting the experimental results. In this paper, we focus on photon-induced corrections to neutral current Drell-Yan, as well as on the irreducible $γγ\to l^+l^-$ background. We present the implementation of the photon-initiated contributions in the Z_ew-BMNNPV Monte Carlo generator for Drell-Yan production at NLO QCD + NLO EW accuracy matched to QED and QCD parton showers within the POWHEG framework. We discuss phenomenological results for the dilepton invariant-mass distribution and the forward-backward asymmetry in the Z-resonance region and in the TeV range.

titles.title: Photon induced corrections to Drell-Yan production in POWHEG

abstracts.value: We determine the loss of mechanical angular momentum $L^μ_{\rm loss}$ of two gravitationally scattering bodies at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ using worldline quantum field theory (WQFT). The gravitational memory effect, a phenomenon of the early- and late-time behaviour of the gravitational field, leads to static contributions to $L^μ_{\rm loss}$. We illuminate how these arise: the linear memory contributes through so-called static correlators, while the nonlinear memory vanishes at this order due to symmetry considerations. The computation of the remaining, dynamical part resembles that of the $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ impulse. We generate its integrand using a reformulation of the WQFT Feynman rules that conserves four-momentum at every vertex and plainly exhibits the classical loops. The three-loop integrals are reduced to master integrals, whose differential equations and boundary matching in the post-Newtonian limit we describe in some detail. In contrast to conservative effects at this order, only polylogarithms appear. While individual contributions to the dynamical part are divergent, these cancel in $L^μ_{\rm loss}$. The quadratic-in-radiation part of our result reproduces earlier results, while the complete result agrees with existing post-Newtonian results.

titles.title: Mechanical angular momentum loss at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ from static and radiative gravitons

abstracts.value: We present an updated analysis of non-standard neutrino self-interactions, where the interaction is effectively mediated by a heavy particle, using the latest available data from DESI and the CMB. The considered data include combinations of DESI DR1 full-shape galaxy clustering (FS), BAO distance measurements, Lyman-$α$ 1D power spectra (Ly-$α$), and a combined CMB likelihood (CMB-SPA) using data from Planck, ACT, and SPT. First, we probe two DESI DR1-only datasets, where the effective interaction parameter $G_{\rm eff}$ is multimodal in the profile likelihood, leading us to analyze two different regimes: moderately interacting (MI$_ν$) and strongly interacting (SI$_ν$) neutrinos. With FS+BAO, the evidence disfavors the SI$_ν$ mode, a trend that becomes slightly stronger with the inclusion of Ly-$α$. However, in the latter dataset, the MI$_ν$ region shows a bimodality in which the intermediate mode is very sharp and peaks around $G_{\rm eff\,} \simeq 10^{-3} \mathrm{MeV}^{-2}$; interestingly, this mode is not penalized versus the weaker standard-like mode. Furthermore, we test CMB and DESI joint data and show that the SI$_ν$ mode is more disfavored by CMB-SPA than by Planck-only data. In particular, the evidence against this mode becomes the strongest thus far (with odds of 5:100000) in the FS+BAO+CMB-SPA combination.

titles.title: Neutrino self-interactions in light of DESI and CMB-SPA

abstracts.value: We investigate dark matter (DM) interpretations of the Galactic Center Excess (GCE) using 17.7 years of Fermi-LAT data and the FL16Y source catalog. We test 80 Galactic diffuse-emission models and include correlated systematic uncertainties from Galactic-plane control regions. We derive combined 95% CL annihilation limits from 30 dwarf spheroidal galaxies (dSphs), including $J$-factor uncertainties, and compare the GCE-preferred regions with these limits and AMS-02 antiproton bounds. For self-conjugate DM, we study two-body annihilation, effective $4b$, $4τ$, and $2b2τ$ channels, and cascades through on-shell scalar mediators. For Model X, the best-fitting diffuse-emission model in our template analysis including a DM component, the dSph limits exclude the 68% CL GCE regions for $b\bar b$, $c\bar c$, light quarks, gluons, and effective $4b$ and $2b2τ$. Parts of the $τ^+τ^-$ and effective $4τ$ regions remain compatible, although their best-fit points exceed these limits. Heavy two-body final states are less constrained but fit the GCE less well. Mediator masses affect both the preferred regions and the constraints. Part of the 68% CL $4b$ cascade region remains below the dSph limits for $r=m_{\rm mediator}/m_{\rm DM}\lesssim0.4$. Among the four-body benchmarks, $4τ$ retains a comparatively large preferred region compatible with dSph and antiproton bounds. With the adopted BIG propagation model, antiproton bounds are generally weaker but constrain part of the $4b$ cascade region. Finally, we examine a secluded singlet fermionic DM benchmark with a predominantly four-bottom cascade.

titles.title: Dark Matter Interpretations of the Galactic Center Gamma-Ray Excess with 18 Years of Fermi-LAT Data and the FL16Y Source Catalog

abstracts.value: We develop a first-principles description of the linearized gravitational field of localized sources in spatially flat Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker universes with arbitrary smooth expansion histories. The construction determines the complete retarded metric and the induced perturbation of the surrounding cosmic fluid from prescribed source stresses and a cosmologically stationary past field. It includes all multipole orders and accounts for curvature tails, through which the field depends on the source's past history inside the light cone. Generalizing the Blanchet-Damour multipolar formalism, we identify gauge-invariant mass and current moments together with a canonical cosmic fluid moment that determines an independent scalar response. This response vanishes in Minkowski and pure de Sitter spacetime, although curvature tails persist in de Sitter. The gauge-invariant multipoles are obtained directly in position space. This gives an exterior description without the nonlocal spatial projection through the source interior required by the usual scalar-vector-tensor decomposition. We also relate the canonical multipole metric to the standard variables of cosmological perturbation theory. The retarded construction requires neither a slow-motion nor a geometric-optics approximation. We define effective multipolar sources by truncating the moments of slowly varying sub-Hubble extended sources at a prescribed Cartesian multipole order, recovering the earlier quadrupolar and octupolar models in de Sitter spacetime. We recover the known Minkowski and de Sitter multipolar fields and obtain an analytical representation for gravitational propagation in the $Λ$CDM model including radiation.

titles.title: Cosmological perturbations from localized sources: a gauge-invariant multipolar theory

abstracts.value: The Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment (P-ONE) is a planned cubic-kilometer-scale neutrino telescope that will be deployed in the Pacific Ocean, leveraging deep-sea infrastructure operated by Ocean Networks Canada (ONC). The first detector line will deploy 320 3-inch Hamamatsu R14374-10 photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) to detect Cherenkov light produced by charged particles propagating through water, as well as light from calibration sources and optical backgrounds. This article presents the systematic characterization of all PMTs to be integrated into the first detector line prior to deployment, ensuring compliance with all detector acceptance criteria. All PMTs satisfy the specified performance criteria: the average transit-time spread (TTS) was measured to be $1.73\pm 0.15\,$ns, and the average charge resolution at a gain of \num{5e6} was $0.43\pm 0.03\,$pC; the average after-pulse rate was measured to be around 6$\,\%$. The integrated P-ONE data acquisition (DAQ) system was also tested and cross-validated against a laboratory digitization system. The second part of the paper presents an in-depth characterization of a subset of six PMTs, focusing on the key properties required for detector simulations, including linearity, after-pulse rate, quantum efficiency, and relative collection efficiency. PMT linearity was measured at a gain of \num{5e6} using the complete P-ONE readout electronics, and the response was found to remain linear for signals up to 150 photoelectrons. After-pulse contributions from $\text{Cs}^{+}$, $\text{He}^{+}$, and other ions were identified in the subset. The peak quantum efficiency was measured to be $27.0\pm0.7\,\%$ at 395 nm. Using measurements of the relative detection efficiency, the collection efficiency was found to differ by a wavelength-independent offset of 10--15$\%$ across the measured wavelength range.

titles.title: Characterization of the R14374-10 photomultiplier tube for the Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment

abstracts.value: We present the calculations of the pion and $η$ meson gravitational form factors (GFFs) from the evaluation of generalized parton distribution functions at non-zero skewness within the graviton soft-wall (GSW) model of hadron structure. Results for the pion have been successfully compared with lattice data for both the $A$ and $D$ GFFs. From these quantities, the mechanical properties of the pion, i.e., the pressure, shear-force, normal and tangential force distributions have been also investigated. Finally, we study also the $η$ meson GFFs to predict and observe differences between the pion and $η$ structures in the corresponding mechanical properties within the GSW model.

abstracts.value: Heavy dark sectors may evade direct production at current colliders while leaving measurable imprints in precision observables and dark matter searches. We study leptophilic scalar dark matter within the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT), considering both real and complex scalar dark matter coupled to vector-like leptonic mediators. We perform the complete one-loop matching of the model onto the dimension-six Warsaw basis and combine the resulting precision constraints with predictions for direct and indirect detection. We compute the relic abundance including coannihilations with the mediator, Sommerfeld enhancement, bound-state formation, and one-loop corrections to scalar dark matter annihilation. We also derive the effective dark matter-photon interactions relevant for nuclear recoils, retaining the full dependence on the dark matter and mediator masses and extending previous results beyond the heavy-mediator limit. We find that global SMEFT fits provide competitive constraints for dark matter masses up to approximately $850$ GeV, while direct detection becomes particularly powerful for compressed spectra. The complex scalar scenario is strongly constrained by the charge-radius interaction, whereas real scalar dark matter remains viable across a substantial region of parameter space. Finally, we show that a modified cosmological expansion history can significantly shift the relic-density-compatible parameter space, thereby changing the complementarity among the different probes.

abstracts.value: We investigate the high-energy behavior of observables sensitive to the production of a Higgs boson in association with a singly charmed hadron at the $\sqrt{s}=14$ TeV LHC, with light-flavored hadrons considered for comparison. Our reference formalism is the hybrid factorization at NLL/NLO$^+$, where the standard collinear picture is enhanced by the resummation of energy logarithms at the next-to-leading level and beyond. We present a prime phenomenological application of the next-to-leading correction to the singly off-shell Higgs emission function, as implemented in the multimodular JETHAD interface, a core element to test the stability of our high-energy distributions under energy-scale variations and to assess the weight of missing higher-order uncertainties. The resulting natural stability traces our path towards precision studies of Higgs production within high-energy next-to-leading-order QCD.

abstracts.value: The statistical long-range Ising (LRI) model in one dimension provides a family of some of the simplest non-exactly solvable critical points. These critical points are described by long-range conformal field theories (CFTs) that are well understood analytically with perturbative expansions and some exact results. Guided by this, we revisit the Monte Carlo (MC) approach to the corresponding lattice model which has many favorable features compared to other systems studied with MC methods. In particular, with very modest computational cost, we are able to estimate scaling dimensions of leading and subleading operators as well as the associated three-point functions, and even certain four-point functions. These results help highlight the fact that 1d LRI CFTs are a phenomenal playground to more generally test non-perturbative methods and ideas for strongly coupled CFTs.

titles.title: Field theory guides Monte Carlo in the one-dimensional long-range Ising model

abstracts.value: We study three-dimensional $BF$ theory as the large-level limit of the doubled Chern--Simons theory $G_k\times G_{-k}$ for simply connected, compact, simple $G$, a limit that connects the symmetry topological field theories of finite and continuous symmetries. Lines whose two highest weights grow linearly with $k$ at fixed difference become $BF$ lines, with magnetic flux set by their average and electric charge equal to their difference. Representing level-$k$ torus states as normalized flux--charge wave packets, we prove that every fixed modular transformation of any fixed normalizable state with regular flux converges in the strong-$*$ topology to its $BF$ counterpart. The Dehn twist gives each line exactly its Aharonov--Bohm phase at every level, while $S$ converges to a Fourier transform exchanging flux and charge, without escaping to singular holonomies or large charges. States that approach singular fluxes at large $k$ are not covered. The natural boundary 2d theory is speculated to be a decompactified boson in the abelian case $G=U(1)$, and $\dim G$ non-compact free scalars for general $G$. For $SU(2)$, we discuss the gapped interfaces between adjacent levels, which must shift some flux or charge by a finite amount. In the $k\rightarrow\infty$ limit the interface is conjectured to be the $c=1$ Runkel--Watts theory.

titles.title: Large-Level Limit of Doubled Chern-Simons Theory Part I: Regular Sector, Boundaries and Interfaces

abstracts.value: Transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) parton distributions provide a three-dimensional description of the momentum structure of hadrons. They are probed in proton-proton and proton-nucleus collisions at the LHC and RHIC, and are a central part of the physics program of the future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). While TMD factorization is well established at moderate Bjorken $x$, the small-$x$ regime requires a different treatment, since large logarithms of $1/x$ must be resummed and non-linear effects due to high gluon densities become important. The Color Glass Condensate (CGC) effective theory provides a natural framework to describe TMDs in this saturation regime and to connect them with standard TMD factorization. This chapter reviews quark and gluon TMDs at small $x$, covering operator definitions, gauge-link structures, and Wilson-line correlators in the CGC for unpolarized and polarized distributions. We discuss factorization for inclusive and diffractive observables, highlighting the role of process dependence and the emergence of a limited set of Wilson-line operators. We then summarize the evolution of these distributions, namely the resummation of logarithms of $1/x$ by the Balitsky-Kovchegov and JIMWLK equations, and of Sudakov logarithms of the hard scale through Collins-Soper-Sterman evolution. We also review TMDs beyond the eikonal approximation, including the sub-eikonal Wilson-line operators that give access to helicity and other spin-dependent distributions, their double-logarithmic small-$x$ evolution and the resulting asymptotics, and the sub-eikonal corrections to the eikonal distributions, which provide a first step toward the moderate-$x$ regime. Finally, we discuss phenomenological implications for present and future experiments, with emphasis on the EIC, and outline the theoretical challenges toward a unified description of TMDs.

titles.title: Transverse momentum dependent parton distributions at small $x$

abstracts.value: This thesis investigates the cosmological dynamics of primordial black holes (PBHs) within the Randall--Sundrum Type II braneworld scenario. The work comprises a preliminary discussion on gravitational collapse in the small-black-hole limit at early cosmological epochs, and two principal studies. The first study presents a fully relativistic treatment of PBH accretion in the early Universe, employing Michel accretion theory within the covariant Shiromizu--Maeda--Sasaki formalism. The analysis reveals that higher-dimensional effects substantially enhance early-time accretion onto light PBHs, with discrepancies between our black hole masses and previous estimates growing with cosmic time as $t^{0.33}$--- a difference that reaches several orders of magnitude by the end of the strong-accretion epoch. This finding fundamentally alters the mapping between the initial PBH mass spectrum and present-day populations. The second study reassesses the observational and cosmological constraints on higher-dimensional PBHs in Randall--Sundrum cosmologies. Constraints from direct Hawking radiation, unresolved diffuse gamma-ray backgrounds, microlensing surveys, and energy injection into the cosmic microwave background are reanalysed in light of the modified higher-dimensional evaporation dynamics and updated observational surveys. Taken together, these results identify viable regions of parameter space in which PBHs can account for the entirety of dark matter while remaining consistent with current observational bounds. Notably, due to the enhanced accretion epoch, PBHs capable of constituting a significant fraction of dark matter may originate from masses below the effective four-dimensional Planck scale. This thesis thus puts forward a dark matter candidate with a distinct evolutionary history and observational signatures today.

titles.title: Primordial black holes in braneworld gravity: A gateway to hidden dimensions and the dark Universe

abstracts.value: The field of Deep Inelastic Scattering is introduced with particular reference to the High Energy Ring Accelerator HERA. The formalism of the Quark Parton Model and its extension in perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics is outlined, defining the concept of a Parton Distribution Function. The HERA data on inclusive and semi-inclusive processes are reviewed with particular emphasis on results at low x and low Q 2 . Their theoretical imterpretation in terms of conventional QCD DGLAP evolution and its extension to BFKL evolution in the low-x regime is explored together with the possibility of the onset of a new non-linear regime which may lead to gluon saturation. The focus then moves to diffractive processes both quasi-elastic and diffractive dissociation, where more detailed hints of saturation are found.

abstracts.value: We study the charge balance function $B(Δη,Δϕ)$ and the charge-dependent transverse-momentum balance function $P_{2}^{\rm CD}(Δη,Δϕ)$ in proton--proton ($pp$) collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$~TeV using \texttt{PYTHIA~8.315} with the Monash tune. Flattenicity is employed as an event-shape observable to probe how these correlations depend on the topology of particle production. The results are examined across different charged-particle multiplicity intervals to disentangle the effects of overall event activity and event topology on $B$ and $P_{2}^{\rm CD}$. Both observables exhibit pronounced near-side correlations around $(Δη,Δϕ)\approx(0,0)$. The near-side peaks become stronger with increasing charged-particle multiplicity, and the RMS widths of both observables decrease systematically, indicating that the correlations become more localized in relative pseudorapidity and azimuth. A clear dependence on flattenicity is also observed: jet-like events (low flattenicity) generally exhibit stronger and narrower near-side correlations than isotropic events (high flattenicity). This event-shape dependence is more pronounced for $P_{2}^{\rm CD}$ than for $B$, indicating that $P_{2}^{\rm CD}$ is more sensitive to event topology, whereas $B$ primarily probes charge-dependent particle-pair correlations. These results demonstrate the complementary nature of the two observables and the potential of flattenicity-based event selection for studying particle-production mechanisms in high-multiplicity $pp$ collisions.

titles.title: Flattenicity dependence of charge and transverse-momentum balance functions in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13.6$ TeV with PYTHIA8

abstracts.value: We investigate a quantum relaxation mechanism for the vacuum energy density arising from the spontaneous symmetry breaking (SSB) $SO(1,4)\to SO(1,3)$, driven by a Higgs field $Φ$ in a MacDowell--Mansouri pre-geometric gravity framework. The theory predicts a countably infinite set of vacua, corresponding to distinct topological sectors, for a periodic Higgs potential with intervening barriers. This structure gives rise to a series of dualities and see-saw relations connecting fundamental scales---the Planck mass and the Cosmological Constant---to topological parameters such as the Gauss-Bonnet coupling and the $θ$-term, all of which emerge only after SSB. A striking consequence is the quantization of the vacuum energy into discrete levels. Starting from a vacuum expectation value $\langle Φ\rangle = v_1$ associated with a large vacuum energy, the system evolves via quantum tunneling through the infinite landscape of minima. Crucially, we demonstrate that the transition probability is maximized for the ordered sequence $ Λ_1 > \cdots > Λ_k > \cdots$, where the Cosmological Constant decreases monotonically toward the asymptotic attractor $Λ_\infty = 0$.

titles.title: Quantum Relaxation Dynamics of Vacuum Energy from Pre-Geometric Gravity

abstracts.value: We propose an $SU(3)$ flavor-filtering strategy to resolve the two-pole structure associated with the $D_0^*(2300)$ and to probe its flavor-sextet component directly in invariant-mass distributions. In unitarized chiral dynamics, the two poles originate predominantly from different irreducible representations of the coupled $\mathcal{D}Φ$ system. We show that the strong decays $Υ\to\barΞ_{c}^{(\prime)}Λ(1520)\mathcal{D}Φ$ and the weak decays $Ξ_{b}^{(\prime)}\toπ^-Λ(1520)\mathcal{D}Φ$ provide approximately antitriplet- and sextet-selective production sources. The predicted $Dπ$, $Dη$, and $D_s\bar K$ spectra exhibit complementary signatures: the higher pole near $2.45~\mathrm{GeV}$ generates a characteristic enhancement between the $Dη$ and $D_s\bar K$ thresholds and a pronounced near-threshold structure in the sextet-favored channels, whereas the lower pole near $2.1~\mathrm{GeV}$ dominates the antitriplet-favored channels. The contrast between these line shapes directly reflects the flavor representation selected by the corresponding cascade-baryon tag. The $Υ$ modes therefore provide experimentally testable observables for establishing the two-pole nature of the $D_0^*(2300)$ and for identifying a charmed-meson resonance with a dominant flavor-sextet component, while the weak-decay analysis tests the robustness of the line-shape pattern against changes in the production mechanism.

titles.title: Probing the two-pole structure of the $D_0^*(2300)$ with an $SU(3)$ flavor filter

abstracts.value: Massive scalar fields can form long-lived clouds outside a black hole, creating a gravitational analog of atomic energy levels. We study such clouds around a charged black hole whose electromagnetic field is modified by Euler–Heisenberg vacuum-polarization effects. We consider both neutral and charged particles, together with different angular and radial excitations. When the particle and black hole have opposite charges, electrostatic attraction strengthens the binding and increases absorption by the horizon. Like charges instead produce more diffuse clouds with energies closer to the rest-mass threshold and substantially longer lifetimes. The nonlinear electromagnetic correction generally weakens the binding and reduces the horizon leakage, although the most weakly bound states are almost insensitive to it. Higher radial levels likewise lie farther from the black hole and decay more slowly. All states found here are decaying, because the localized levels remain well separated from the superradiant frequency range. The particle charge therefore controls the broad organization of the spectrum, while nonlinear vacuum polarization leaves a smaller but systematic imprint on both the level energies and their lifetimes.

titles.title: Charged gravitational atoms in Euler–Heisenberg electrodynamics: quasi-bound states of charged particles around black holes

abstracts.value: Characterizing complex quantum evolutions in the microscopic world is crucial for understanding fundamental physics and advancing quantum information applications. In conventional quantum process tomography, individual process matrix elements are obtained indirectly through reconstruction. Here, we use sequential system-ancilla couplings and quantum erasure to directly access these elements for arbitrary quantum processes. Within the pseudo-density-matrix framework, these operations realize an effective erasure-based closed timelike curve (E-CTC) interaction. During E-CTC-assisted measurements, the protocol combines selective computational-basis addressing with fixed superposition preparation and projections. Although the configuration count is not reduced for general processes, these fixed settings can simplify control when computational-basis states are readily addressable. We experimentally demonstrate our scheme in a photonic platform by characterizing several two- and four-dimensional quantum processes with average fidelities above <math><mrow><mn>99</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow></math>. Our work offers a basis-rotation-free approach to high-dimensional quantum process characterization within the erasure-based CTC framework.

titles.title: Direct quantum process characterization via erasure-based closed timelike curves

abstracts.value: Proton-induced reactions on <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>19</mn></mmultiscripts></math> can lead to different branches of the CNO cycles, possibly resulting in the synthesis of heavier nuclei. For instance, CNO breakout is considered to be a viable path to the production of calcium in the most metal-poor stars. Present-day observational studies indicate that <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>19</mn></mmultiscripts></math> is mostly produced in the asymptotic giant branch phase of low- and intermediate-mass stars, and its synthesis and surface abundance are strictly intertwined with the production of heavy elements through slow neutron captures (s-process). Therefore, <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>19</mn></mmultiscripts></math> can act as a probe of nucleosynthesis scenarios and stars inner structure. In recent years, new experimental data on <math><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>19</mn></mmultiscripts></math> destruction reactions have been published, highlighting the occurrence of several resonances at astrophysical energies close to the proton threshold. While direct measurements relied on extrapolation from higher energies, indirect measurements made it possible to cover the astrophysical energies. In this work we will focus on the threshold region, which has been studied by means of the Trojan Horse method (THM) in the framework of the modified <math><mi>R</mi></math>-matrix approach. Thanks to this novel measurement, we could derive the asymptotic normalization coefficient (ANC) of the <math><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>448</mn></mrow></math> keV subthreshold resonance and the strength of the 11 keV one, which turned out to be significantly lower than previously extrapolated. To evaluate the astrophysical impact, we calculated the astrophysical reaction rates using a modern Monte Carlo approach, constraining them with the ANC and threshold resonance strengths measured via the THM.

abstracts.value: Collective subradiant states, characterized by strongly suppressed radiative decay, provide a promising platform for quantum information storage. A particularly attractive application is the storage of arbitrary qubit states, enabled by the long lifetimes of these collective excitations. Yet their intrinsically weak coupling to propagating modes poses a major obstacle to high-efficiency, high-fidelity photon storage and retrieval. Here we present a waveguide-QED protocol that overcomes this limitation in a chain of emitters by dynamically modulating their resonance frequencies. This temporal control tailors the collective decay rates, allowing single-photon pulses to efficiently excite subradiant states and to be deterministically converted into long-lived dark states. By programming spatial detuning patterns, we show that arbitrary time-bin qubit states can be mapped on demand onto two orthogonal dark states. These results establish a scalable route to subradiant-state-based quantum memories and open opportunities for integrated quantum photonic devices.

titles.title: Deterministic quantum states storage via dynamical control of subradiant states

abstracts.value: Bell nonlocality is an intrinsic feature of quantum mechanics, which can be detected via the violation of Bell inequalities. It is therefore a fundamental question to certify Bell nonlocality from experimental data. Here we present an optimization framework to detect Bell-operator correlations by exploring flexible mappings between Bell inequalities and Hamiltonians corresponding to the Bell operators. We show that several Hamiltonian models can be mapped to new inequalities with improved classical bounds compared to the original one, enabling a more robust certification of Bell-operator correlations. From the other direction, we investigate the mapping from fixed Bell inequalities to Hamiltonians, aiming to maximize quantum violations while considering experimental imperfections. As a practical application, we experimentally exploit this method in an XXZ-like honeycomb-lattice model utilizing over 70 superconducting qubits. The successful application of this technique, together with the combination of the two directions to form an optimization loop, may open new avenues for developing more practical and noise-resilient certification techniques for Bell-operator correlations and enable broader experimental explorations.

titles.title: Improved certification of Bell-operator correlations via optimization

When Graph Autoencoders Look the Wrong Way:
Complexity Bias and Simple Baselines in Unsupervised
Anomaly Detection on the LHC Olympics 2020 Dataset

Jamil Khan1

Independent researcher; undergraduate student in Computer Engineering
ORCID: 0009-0007-1762-0416

Abstract

Graph autoencoders (GAEs) trained only on background are a natural candidate for model-
agnostic new-physics searches. I tested two of them on the LHC Olympics 2020 R&D dataset,
where a W ′ → XY → (qq̄)(qq̄) dijet resonance is hidden in QCD background. The first is
a node-level GAE that scores per-particle reconstruction error. The second encodes the
whole event, reconstructs it with a set decoder and a Chamfer loss, and offers three scores:
reconstruction error, latent k-nearest-neighbour distance and latent Gaussian-mixture likeli-
hood. The decision criterion was fixed before looking at any test result. Neither model beats
simple label-free observables. The node-level model reaches an AUC of 0.483 ± 0.005 with
max-reduction and 0.781 with mean-reduction; all three event-level scores are inverted, with
AUCs between 0.401 and 0.436, stable across seeds, nine ablations, and signal-contaminated
training. By contrast, the mean transverse momentum per particle, ⟨pT⟩ = HT/N , reaches
0.811, and −τ21 of the leading jet reaches 0.801. Correlation and binned analyses indicate
that the latent-density scores track event complexity: the signal has fewer, harder particles
than QCD and is therefore placed in dense regions of the learned manifold. The benchmark
code is public, and I suggest ⟨pT⟩ as a standard reference baseline for unsupervised methods
on this dataset.

Code and data: https://github.com/Viverun/Hidden-Vertex
Archived version: doi:10.5281/zenodo.23432779

1khanjamilahmed202@gmail.com

https://orcid.org/0009-0007-1762-0416
https://github.com/Viverun/Hidden-Vertex
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23432779
mailto:khanjamilahmed202@gmail.com


1 Introduction
Searches for physics beyond the Standard Model (BSM) at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC)
are mostly designed around specific signal hypotheses. Model-agnostic anomaly detection aims
to complement them by flagging events that are atypical with respect to the Standard Model
background, without assuming a signal model. The LHC Olympics 2020 (LHCO) [1] established
a common benchmark for this task, and autoencoders, in which events with large reconstruction
error are treated as anomalous, are among the most widely studied unsupervised approaches [2–
5].

Autoencoder scores have a known weakness: they can end up measuring how complex an
input is rather than how unusual it is. For jet images, simple signal jets turn out to be easier
to reconstruct than QCD jets [4]. This project started as an attempt to build a working graph-
based detector, and ran into the same problem for particle graphs of whole events. This paper
documents what happened:

1. a reproducible benchmark harness on the public LHCO R&D data, with a frozen test set,
multi-seed runs, bootstrap confidence intervals and within-bin AUCs that test whether a
score carries information beyond trivial event quantities;

2. a set of label-free reference baselines, among which the mean transverse momentum per
particle, ⟨pT⟩ = HT/N , is the strongest particle-level observable (AUC 0.811), above HT,
mjj , and a node-level GAE;

3. a negative result, under a decision rule fixed in advance, for an event-level GAE whose three
anomaly scores are systematically inverted, with ablations, a contamination study, and a
correlation-based diagnosis that links the latent-density inversion to event complexity.

None of this is a working anomaly detector. The practical point is simpler: before claiming that
an unsupervised model has learned something on this dataset, compare it with ⟨pT⟩. If it cannot
beat a ratio of two event totals, it has probably only learned the energy and multiplicity scale.

2 Dataset and test protocol
I use the LHCO 2020 R&D dataset [1, 6]. Background consists of QCD dijet events and signal
of W ′ → XY with mW ′ = 3.5 TeV, mX = 500 GeV and mY = 100 GeV, each of X and
Y decaying to two quarks. Events were generated with Pythia 8 [7] and the Delphes 3 [8]
detector simulation, and are stored as up to 700 hadrons (pT, η, ϕ). Jet-level features (anti-kt [9]
R = 1 jet masses, N -subjettiness ratios [10] and mjj) are taken from the accompanying feature
file.

One practical warning first: the publicly available file events_anomalydetection_v2.h5 is
sorted: rows 0–999,999 are background and rows ≥ 1,000,000 are signal. Any pipeline that
reads a prefix of the file therefore sees no signal at all; I select events explicitly by row index.
The test set is frozen across all experiments: 5,000 background events (rows 40,000–44,999) and
5,000 signal events (rows 1,000,000–1,004,999). Models are trained on 180,000 background-only
events (rows ≥ 45,000) with a 20,000-event background validation set.

Metrics. I report the ROC AUC with bootstrap confidence intervals over the 10,000 test
events (95% for baselines; 98.3% for the three model scores, a Bonferroni correction for three
comparisons). To test whether a score carries information beyond trivial event quantities, I also
compute the AUC within bins of HT, particle multiplicity N , and leading-particle pT. The sign
of every score (“larger = more anomalous”) is fixed in advance.

(5k signal, 5k background), with 95% bootstrap intervals and the minimum AUC within bins of

AUC is 0.483 ± 0.005.

Decision criterion. Before any test result for the event-level model, I fixed the following gate:
a model score passes only if the lower bound of its seed-averaged AUC interval exceeds the best
particle-level baseline, and its minimum within-bin AUC is at least 0.6.

3 Models
Node-level GAE. Each event is a radius graph with edges between particles at ∆R < 0.4. A
graph convolutional encoder [11] compresses each particle’s features to a one-dimensional latent
and a decoder reconstructs its standardized (pT, η, ϕ); the model has 420 effective parameters.
The event score is the maximum or the mean of the per-particle reconstruction errors.

Event-level GAE. The encoder applies three residual neighbour-averaging layers of width 64
on the same ∆R < 0.4 graph, followed by concatenated mean, max and pT-weighted pooling
into a 16-dimensional event latent. A set decoder reconstructs the K = 48 hardest particles
and is trained with a symmetric Chamfer distance [12], which is invariant to particle ordering.
Events are truncated to the 350 hardest particles, a cut chosen from the measured multiplicity
distribution before training (0.7% of background and 0.02% of signal events exceed it). The
model has 95,888 parameters and is trained for 30 epochs with AdamW (learning rate 10−3,
batch size 256, early-stopping patience 5) on one NVIDIA T4 GPU, about 18 minutes per seed.
Three anomaly scores are evaluated: (i) the Chamfer reconstruction error; (ii) the mean distance
to the 20 nearest training latents; and (iii) the negative log-likelihood of the latent under an
8-component Gaussian mixture fitted to training latents.

4 Results

4.1 Reference baselines

Table 1 lists label-free event observables evaluated on the frozen test set. The harness reproduces
my earlier node-level numbers exactly (HT 0.792, mjj 0.788, node-level GAE 0.478/0.781, each
inside its interval). The strongest particle-level observable is ⟨pT⟩ (AUC 0.811), which exceeds
HT because it combines the higher energy scale of signal with its lower multiplicity (mean
N = 140 for signal vs. 182 for background). The mass-window score −|mjj − 3500 GeV| (AUC
0.900) requires knowledge of the signal and is shown only as an oracle reference.

2

For the node-level GAE, the choice of reduction matters more than the model: the same
trained network gives 0.48 with max and 0.78 with mean. Across five seeds, the max-reduction
AUC is 0.483 ± 0.005. Scaling the network by 44× in parameters lowers the training loss by
about 2% and leaves the AUC unchanged. The max score is dominated by the hardest particle
(Spearman ρ = 0.70 with leading pT, and AUC 0.38–0.47 within leading-pT deciles). Since a
per-particle MLP with the same one-dimensional bottleneck reconstructs pT almost perfectly,
the residual error originates in the neighbourhood averaging of the graph convolution. The
mean score retains AUC 0.61–0.82 within deciles of HT, N and leading pT, but it is strongly
anti-correlated with multiplicity (ρ = −0.71) and does not exceed ⟨pT⟩.

4.2 Event-level GAE

Table 2 summarises the headline result. All three scores lie significantly below 0.5, and the gate
is not passed. The seed-to-seed spread (0.01–0.02) is small compared with the distance to 0.5, so
the inversion is systematic. Training was stable, with agreement between training and validation
loss and no latent collapse.

Figure 1 compares all scores. Every model score lies below the simplest particle-level observ-
ables.

4.3 Ablations and contamination

Nine variations of the event-level model, each with two seeds, were run as a sensitivity analysis
and not used to select a configuration (Table 3). None produces a useful score; the best single
value is 0.502 (Chamfer, K = 24), i.e. chance. Training on background contaminated with
1% signal changes the scores by at most ∼ 0.015, which is inconclusive with one seed. At 9%
contamination, the signal fraction of the R&D file, the density scores become more inverted
(kNN 0.362, GMM 0.387), consistent with signal events making signal-like regions of the latent
space denser.

5 Diagnosis
Table 4 gives Spearman correlations of the seed-0 scores with simple event quantities. The latent-
density scores increase with multiplicity (ρ = +0.28 for kNN, +0.23 for GMM) and decrease
with ⟨pT⟩ (−0.27, −0.20), also within background alone. Their AUC within multiplicity bins is
close to chance (kNN 0.43–0.50, GMM 0.47–0.51). Since signal events have fewer and harder
particles than QCD background, they fall into dense regions of a latent space trained on QCD.
Under the pre-declared sign (far from training data means anomalous), this produces AUCs
below 0.5. This explanation is supported by correlations but was not tested causally.

The Chamfer score behaves differently: it barely tracks multiplicity (ρ = +0.08) or ⟨pT⟩
(ρ = −0.07), and remains inverted within multiplicity bins (0.41–0.48) and within HT bins
(down to 0.31). Its inversion is therefore not explained by multiplicity alone, and its origin
remains open. The three scores are only moderately correlated with one another (Chamfer–
kNN 0.53, Chamfer–GMM 0.42, kNN–GMM 0.87). Flipping the sign post hoc would give AUCs
of 0.56–0.60, still far below ⟨pT⟩. I mention this only to show that the scores contain a weak
complexity signal rather than noise; it is not a result.

6 Discussion and outlook
These results add to the evidence that autoencoder-based anomaly scores are vulnerable to
complexity bias [4], and extend it to particle-graph representations of full events. Two practical
lessons follow. First, unsupervised methods on the LHCO R&D data should be compared not

kNN −0.02 / +0.19 / 0.00 +0.28 / +0.30 / +0.19 −0.02 / −0.05 / +0.05 −0.27 / −0.24 / −0.20

only with HT but with ⟨pT⟩, which already reaches AUC 0.81 without any training. Second,
within-bin AUCs at fixed multiplicity and HT are a cheap and informative diagnostic: a score
that loses its discrimination at fixed complexity has not learned substructure.

The features that distinguish the signal in this dataset are jet-level: two-prong substructure
(τ21), jet masses and mjj . These are not available to the encoder as explicit inputs. Natural next
steps are therefore (i) adding jet-level and substructure inputs, (ii) conditioning the model on,
or regressing out, multiplicity and ⟨pT⟩ so that the score measures structure at fixed complexity,
and (iii) choosing the score sign on background-only or simulated data. Large foundation models
for collider physics trained on simulated events are expected to face the same issue. Benchmarks
of the kind released here can be used to check whether their anomaly scores capture more than
event complexity.

Limitations. All results use a single signal model and the R&D dataset, not the LHCO black
boxes. The event-level model was evaluated in one configuration fixed in advance with limited
ablations, and the complexity explanation is correlational. Ablation and contamination runs
use two or one seeds, so differences below ∼ 0.02 should not be interpreted.

Code availability
All code, configurations, and the benchmark harness are available at the public repository https:
//github.com/Viverun/Hidden-Vertex, under the MIT licence. The detailed result reports
are in docs/PART1_VERIFICATION.md and docs/PART2_RESULTS.md.

Acknowledgements

were performed on Kaggle GPU notebooks.

Use of AI tools
AI assistants (Anthropic’s Claude) were used to help with code development, debugging and
editing of the manuscript text. All experiments, results and conclusions were checked by the
author, who takes full responsibility for the content of this paper.

abstracts.value: Reliable quantum computation requires methods for verifying quantum circuits. Level-synchronized tree automata (LSTAs) were recently introduced to represent sets of quantum states for this purpose. We study LSTAs along two axes relevant to verification: the complexity of their decision problems and the size of their representations under circuit operations. We prove that acyclic LSTAs have NP-complete nonemptiness and $Π_2^P$-complete language inclusion, and that general language inclusion is EXPSPACE-complete. We further prove inherent quadratic representation growth under individual quantum gates in a fixed qubit order, and give an adjacent-qubit reordering construction that preserves level synchronization. These results clarify the scope of applicability of the automata-theoretic toolbox for quantum circuit verification.

titles.title: On the Complexity of Level-Synchronized Tree Automata for Quantum Circuit Verification

abstracts.value: Nonrelativistic quantum chemistry is based on the Schrödinger equation in continuous, unbounded space. Computational approaches on classical and quantum computers often truncate the spatial domain and introduce a finite-dimensional basis, reducing the continuum problem to a finite-dimensional one. There is therefore a fundamental question: to what extent does this approximation capture the original continuum problem? In this work, we develop a general Sobolev-Galerkin framework for estimating spatial discretization errors in quantum simulation with unbounded Hamiltonians. We apply this framework to many-body Coulomb systems and establish both periodization and Galerkin error estimates for wave-function dynamics and ground-state energies. For dynamics, the finite-basis projection error of the exact wave function does not capture the full basis-discretization error: an additional dynamical projection error enters our bound at a different rate, and we introduce an inner-product argument to control this contribution. Interestingly, the spatial convergence rates for wave-function dynamics and ground-state energies differ quantitatively. For ground-state energies, we establish a sharp $M^{-1}$ convergence rate at fixed cell size, where $M$ is the number of one-particle basis functions. We also show that a uniform $M^{-1}$ convergence rate is impossible for the corresponding real-time wave-function error with general $H^2$ initial data. The analysis relies on many-body Sobolev estimates with explicit polynomial dependence on system size. Combining these estimates with state-of-the-art quantum algorithms, we obtain, to our knowledge, the first rigorous end-to-end complexity bounds for quantum simulation of molecular and electronic dynamics with all spatial errors explicitly controlled. The number of basis functions is determined directly from the continuum problem, without regularization.

titles.title: Spatial Discretization Error for Quantum Chemistry Simulation

abstracts.value: The realization of fault-tolerant quantum computation relies on Quantum Error-Correcting Codes (QECC). Of particular interest are codes that combine a high encoding rate with sufficient distance. Existing algebraic constructions, such as lifted product (LP) codes, build a large quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) code from a classical base matrix. In this work we introduce LiftDiff, a generative approach to the discovery of QECC. A discrete denoising diffusion model is trained to generate base matrices over the group algebra $\mathbb{F}_2[\mathbb{Z}_\ell]$, which are then expanded into LP codes. The reverse diffusion process is guided by an energy function that evaluates quantum code properties, including girth, degree, sparsity and decoding performance, steering the sampler toward matrices that yield LP codes with favorable parameters. Our method discovers codes with parameters such as $[[169,13,11]]$, $[[143,15,9]]$, and $[[260,24,10]]$, including a $[[247,19,14]]$ code that achieves the highest ${kd^2}/{n}$ among the baselines. Moreover, several discovered codes outperform the Gross code across a broad range of the tested physical error rates under both code-capacity and circuit-level noise.

titles.title: LiftDiff: Guided Discrete Diffusion for Quantum Code Construction

abstracts.value: Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) hardware has transformed quantum computing into a practical experimental platform while introducing fundamental challenges associated with hardware noise, decoherence, and probabilistic execution. Although quantum software testing (QST) has rapidly emerged as an active research area, it remains unclear to what extent existing testing methodologies explicitly engage with noisy and hardware-constrained execution environments. This paper presents a systematic empirical landscape analysis of noise-awareness in QST research through a deterministic, taxonomy-guided analytical framework applied to 61 papers published between 2018 and 2025 across eight testing paradigms, contrasting how contributions are framed with how they are evaluated. Among the analyzed papers, 47 (77.0%) are noise-oblivious and only 14 (23.0%) explicitly engage with noise-related execution concerns, while only 11 (18.0%) report evaluation on physical hardware or a noisy simulator. Test generation, the largest paradigm, exhibits a noise-awareness rate of only 14.3%, and debugging and repair 18.2%; coverage-based, metamorphic, and differential testing contain no noise-aware contributions. Noise-aware methodologies emerged late and remain outnumbered in all analyzed years. Framing and evaluation are strongly associated (odds ratio 40.5, p < 0.001) yet diverge for individual papers: 5 of the 14 noise-aware papers evaluate only on ideal simulators. Inferential statistical tests are reported in only 16.4% of papers. The classification framework was validated against a blinded, human-coded reference sample, achieving almost perfect inter-rater agreement on testing-technique classification and substantial agreement on noise-awareness. The framework provides a reusable empirical basis for longitudinal analysis of hardware-conscious testing practice.

titles.title: Noise-Awareness in Quantum Software Testing: An Empirical Landscape Analysis

abstracts.value: We show positive and negative results on classical relay channels with entanglement assistance, revealing a sharp contrast between strictly causal and causal relay encoding. First, we consider van der Meulen's setting of a unit-delay relay, with strictly causal encoding. We show that the standard cutset upper bound continues to hold with entanglement assistance, and deduce that entanglement does not increase the capacity for several classes of relay channels. Second, we consider a zero-delay relay, where the encoding is causal. We present an example in which entanglement enables rates that exceed the cutset upper bound by at least 12.5%. Namely, entanglement shared between the source and relay significantly increases the capacity of a classical zero-delay relay channel.

titles.title: Can Quantum Entanglement Increase the Capacity of a Classical Relay Channel?

abstracts.value: Wiring and bandwidth bottlenecks between a quantum processor and room-temperature electronics can be reduced by placing digital control at the cryogenic stage, but commercial foundry standard-cell libraries are not specified for operation at 4 K. A cryogenic recharacterization flow is therefore developed for a commercial 22 nm FD-SOI foundry standard-cell library using commercially available cryogenic compact-device models, while retaining the original cell circuits, layouts, logic functions, and implementation semantics and remaining compatible with the commercial synthesis, place-and-route, and signoff methodology used at room temperature. Body-bias dependence is quantified over 38,640 matched slew/load points at zero, +/-0.9 V, and +/-1.8 V body bias. Relative to full bias, zero-bias operation increases the median rising and falling delays by 38.6x and 33.0x, while approximately 90% of transitions exceed the foundry-defined maximum-transition envelope. The 0.8 V-to-0.4 V level shifter is even more sensitive to body bias: its worst-case falling delay decreases from 30.6 ns at zero bias to 0.56 ns at +/-1.8 V. For the outbound 0.4 V-to-0.8 V crossing, driving the 0.8 V receiver without a level shifter dissipates 57.7 uW of static power per bit at full bias, against 0.196 nW when level-shifted. In post-route analysis of the unchanged extracted physical database of a fabricated 32-bit ALU, the register-to-register setup boundary increases from 1.3 MHz at zero bias to 37.9 MHz at +/-0.9 V and 132.9 MHz at +/-1.8 V.

titles.title: Cryogenic Recharacterization of a Commercial 22 nm FD-SOI Foundry Standard-Cell Library

abstracts.value: Inner products of random matrices and random quantum states---such as orbital inner products, expectation values, overlaps, and cyclic Bargmann invariants---are shown to follow from two underlying mechanisms: the diagonal of an induced random state is Dirichlet distributed, and the expectation value of a random pure state in a rank-one or two-by-two operator is a numerical shadow on an elliptical disk. For states induced by an environment of dimension $K$, the expectation value of any observable is a Curry--Schoenberg spline with each eigenvalue repeated $K$ times, and the vector of moments has an explicit density on a simplex; for a qutrit, the variance law is obtained in finite form. The overlap of two random qubit states attains its mode at its mean for every rotation-invariant ensemble, but for Hilbert--Schmidt qutrits the density at the mean has a strictly negative derivative, so mode and mean separate; for large environments, the centred overlap converges to a variance-gamma law rather than a Gaussian. For two noncommuting qubit observables, the joint law of the two standard deviations is derived for all $K$, and the probability of coming within a small distance of the optimal sum of variances scales as a power of that distance, with a different exponent when the Bloch axes are orthogonal. For three Haar-random qubit states, the exact density of the Bargmann invariant is given in terms of a complete elliptic integral, together with its local behaviour and elementary marginals. In every dimension, the probability that its real part is negative---certifying basis-independent coherence---is computed, along with all mixed moments. For cycles of arbitrary length, the invariant is shown to be driven by an exact three-parameter Markov chain, and the logarithm of its modulus obeys a law of large numbers and a central limit theorem.

titles.title: Exact probability laws of random inner products: Dirichlet splines, overlaps, uncertainty, and Bargmann invariants

abstracts.value: We characterize the hybrid Fourier transform on the Schwartz--Grassmann space $\caS(\bbR^m)\otimesΛ_{2n}$ by operator intertwining relations. Using the bosonic oscillator Howe decomposition and the fermionic Lefschetz decomposition, we describe the action of the hybrid Fourier transform on both tensor factors. We show that first-order covariance with respect to coordinate multiplication and differentiation determines the transform up to a scalar. For $m,n\ge1$, we prove that covariance under all even quadratic operators, together with any one nonzero mixed quadratic operator, determines the linear span of the hybrid Fourier transform and its inverse. This rigidity result is obtained by computing the ordinary commutants of the even and full quadratic oscillator actions of $\fosp(4n|2m)$. After a degree-scaling change of normalization, we make the hybrid Fourier transform unitary with respect to the occupation number inner product, and factor it into a bosonic oscillator rotation and (up to a scalar phase) an $SU(2)$ rotation in the fermionic Lefschetz representation. For $m=1$ and $n\ge2$, we show that full even quadratic covariance together with the parity-preserving cubic relation for $qQ_f$ determines the unitary transform up to a global phase and a fermion-parity phase. Finally we calculate the unitary conjugation formulas for Hubbard--Holstein Hamiltonian for a hybrid continuous-variable and discrete-variable quantum system.

titles.title: Super Howe duality and rigidity of hybrid Fourier transforms

abstracts.value: We prove that the random phase approximation provides an upper bound on the correlation energy of a three-dimensional, weakly interacting, Fermi gas in the thermodynamic limit at high density. More precisely, we consider a mean-field scaling regime where the kinetic and interaction Hamiltonian are scaled by $ρ^{-2/3}$ and $ρ^{-1}$, respectively. We use a correlated trial state constructed through a quasi-bosonic Bogoliubov transformation of collective particle--hole excitations associated to patches on the Fermi surface. Key of the proof is to control the position-space localization of the collective excitations. Combined with an iterated Duhamel expansion of the expectation values of (localized) particle number operators we obtain extensive estimates, which justify the reduction to an effective quadratic Hamiltonian and its approximate diagonalization.

titles.title: Upper Bound on the Correlation Energy of a Dense Fermi Gas in the Thermodynamic Limit

abstracts.value: Recent work by Greenblatt, Lange, Marcelli, and Porta (Commun. Math. Phys. 2024) provides the first rigorous justification of adiabatic theory for interacting quantum systems at positive temperature. Their analysis treats weakly interacting lattice fermions and combines a rigorous Wick rotation with fermionic cluster expansion techniques. Here, we study a class of weakly interacting quantum spin systems and derive response theory at positive temperature, thereby covering non-Fermi systems for the first time. Our proof identifies and exploits the locality property of local indistinguishability as a key ingredient in carrying out low-temperature adiabatic expansions. The fact that these systems satisfy local indistinguishability was recently established jointly with Adhikari (arXiv:2508.15907) using cluster expansion methods together with a probabilistic swapping trick.

titles.title: Response theory at low temperature for weakly interacting quantum spin systems

abstracts.value: Consider $N$ identical quantum systems at the vertices of a graph, interacting via pairwise edge couplings. We designate $K$ vertices as a system of interest $\mathrm S$ and the remaining $N-K$ as a reservoir $\mathrm R$. Under generic connectivity assumptions between $\mathrm S$ and $\mathrm R$, we show that for $N\to\infty$, the reduced state of $\mathrm S$ converges to a convex combination of symmetric product states of $K$ single-vertex density matrices -- called a de Finetti representation. Unlike in standard derivations for symmetric (exchangeable) systems, we establish de Finetti representations for quantum networks, which are inherently non-exchangeable. We construct the representations explicitly and quantify the convergence rate. We show that Erdős--Rényi random graphs exhibit the de Finetti structure: as the reservoir grows, the reduced state of any fixed finite subgraph converges almost surely to an explicit deterministic product state. As applications, we establish a general area law for the entanglement entropy of $\mathrm S$, analyze mean-field and fluctuation scalings of the $\mathrm S$-$\mathrm R$ interaction, and illustrate our results on qubit networks. We also derive quantitative convergence estimates for information-theoretic quantities, including von Neumann entropy, mutual information, and entanglement within $\mathrm S$ and between $\mathrm S$ and $\mathrm R$.

titles.title: De Finetti Structures in Networks of Quantum Systems

abstracts.value: We use Neumann's normal form to decide whether the double branched cover of a knot bounds a negative-definite plumbing tree in either orientation, starting from the recognised Seifert or graph-manifold structure of the cover. For many non-alternating knots with at most thirteen crossings whose unknotting numbers were unknown, this identifies the cases in which the Heegaard Floer homology of the cover can be computed from such a plumbing, and shows for most of the others that it cannot. We determine 112 new unknotting numbers. For 43 of them, the lower bound rests on Heegaard Floer homology computed from the plumbing; for the other 69, it comes from linking pairings and from a theorem of McCoy and Park on special alternating knots. Finally, we show that the knot 13n1587 is a further explicit counterexample to the Bernhard--Jablan conjecture, after 13n3370.

titles.title: Negative-Definite Plumbings and New Unknotting Numbers

abstracts.value: Two-band 2D fractional Chern insulators (FCIs) have recently been shown, in principle, to admit unusual anyonic order, associated with Bloch Hopfions localized in momentum space. Here we show that bounding the integrated quantum metric along one primitive Brillouin-zone cycle may refine this topological order to $|C|$ distinct braiding observables, cyclically permuted by lattice translations, for Chern numbers $|C| > 1$. The cyclic structure entails mildly non-abelian braiding phases and otherwise matches the spectral flow exhibited by the FCI's hybrid Wannier states, with the metric bound equivalently a bound on the states' real-space spread. We give a classification of quantum gates in principle implementable on this topological order; among them we find the non-Clifford T-gate and the non-Clifford entangling CCZ-gate. This points to novel pathways to fault-tolerant quantum processes within the known orbital structure of FCIs, potentially informing experimental searches towards hardware for future topological quantum computers.

titles.title: Topological Quantum Gates on FCIs with Bounded Quantum Geometry

abstracts.value: We classify possible topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions with up to 22 anyons in the bosonic case and up to 26 in the fermionic case, through the modular data of modular and supermodular tensor categories. We construct such data via congruence representations of $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ using a numerical optimization algorithm that scales to high rank. We chart the relations between the resulting theories, including anyon condensations and Chern-Simons realizations. We find examples of modular data that do not appear to arise from any Chern-Simons theory by any sequence of condensations of anyons or gaugings of ordinary global symmetries. These examples give qualitatively new topological quantum field theories, which go beyond any notion of gauge theory. For examples in this class with 11 and 12 anyon types, we solve the pentagon and hexagon equations explicitly, showing that these modular data are realized by full unitary topological quantum field theories. We also introduce https://www.AnyonAtlas.org, an online resource for exploring the data.

titles.title: The Anyon Atlas

abstracts.value: We propose a scalable and efficient \textit{in situ} method for assessing the multiparticle indistinguishability of identical bosons or fermions in quantum interference experiments on linear interferometers by harnessing quantum parallelism and the bunching/anti-bunching tendencies of these particles. The proposed certification method can be applied to any generic linear interferometer. For particles occupying distinct input ports of a Haar-random unitary interferometer, the number of experimental runs required to attain a prescribed statistical precision is polynomial in the number of particles, the interferometer size, and the inverse precision, with high probability. Our method is robust under losses: for uniform particle losses, the polynomial scaling is preserved when the inverse single-particle survival probability is polynomially bounded. Our scheme is especially suitable for certifying the indistinguishability of single photons in large-scale interference experiments, such as Boson Sampling in the regime of quantum advantage over classical computation.

titles.title: \textit{In situ} certification of multiparticle indistinguishability in a generic interferometer
